ratings.reviewer_notes: Focused review of Hashimoto's thyroiditis describing VDR-mediated Treg/Th17 regulation and clinical effects of vitamin D supplementation on thyroid antibodies.
Bidirectional Mendelian randomization directly evaluates causality between vitamin D status and TPO antibody concentration, supporting an effect of lower vitamin D on greater thyroid autoimmunity.
Review covers immune-cell vitamin D synthesis, VDR signaling, genetic evidence, and supplementation in autoimmune endocrine diseases including Hashimoto's and Graves' disease.
Focused narrative review links VDR polymorphisms and vitamin D signaling to T-, B-, and dendritic-cell modulation and antibody levels in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Case-control genetic study finds an association between one VDR variant and Graves' disease susceptibility, but does not assess immune-regulatory mechanisms or immune-cell outcomes.

Directly measures vitamin D and multiple inflammatory cytokines in Hashimoto's patients and controls; patients had lower vitamin D and higher cytokines, although the abstract does not report direct vitamin D–cytokine correlation analyses.
Meta-analysis associates VDR polymorphisms with autoimmune thyroid disease risk, providing genetic support for involvement of vitamin D signaling without testing immune regulation.
Examines VDR rs2228570 and vitamin D levels across thyroid pathologies, including autoimmune thyroiditis, but does not measure immune-regulatory outcomes.

Review specifically discusses vitamin D in autoimmune thyroiditis, including VDR expression on immune cells, suppression of Th1 activity and inflammatory cytokines, deficiency, and vitamin D-pathway polymorphisms.
Meta-analysis links several VDR polymorphisms with Hashimoto's or broader autoimmune thyroid disease risk but does not directly evaluate immune modulation.

Focused review describes a proposed mechanism whereby active vitamin D inhibits Th1 cytokine-driven HLA-DR expression on thyrocytes and discusses vitamin D-pathway polymorphisms in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Randomized controlled trial directly tests supplementation in autoimmune thyroid disease and reports a significantly greater reduction in TPO antibody titers with vitamin D.
Double-blind placebo-controlled trial directly tests vitamin D treatment in deficient Hashimoto's patients and finds no significant effect on TPO antibodies or thyroid function.

Relevant negative observational evidence: Hashimoto's thyroiditis was not associated with greater vitamin D deficiency, and vitamin D did not show the expected inverse relationship with thyroid antibodies.

Case-control study directly evaluates vitamin D status, VDR variants, and thyroid autoimmunity, finding more deficiency and an inverse vitamin D–TPO antibody correlation in Hashimoto's but no VDR genotype association.
Focused review synthesizes vitamin D effects on cytokines and Th17/Tr1 subsets, antithyroid antibodies, thyroid function, and other immunological pathways in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Clinical study in women with Hashimoto's reports negative correlations between vitamin D and anti-TPO/anti-TG antibodies, providing observational evidence tied to thyroid autoimmunity.
Broad thyroid-focused review includes vitamin D associations with Hashimoto's, Graves', and postpartum thyroiditis, but the abstract provides little specific evidence about immune regulation.
Human study finds substantially more vitamin D deficiency in autoimmune thyroid disease and associations with antithyroid antibodies and abnormal thyroid function.

Double-blind randomized trial directly measures immune effects of supplementation in Hashimoto's, including CD4+ T-cell cytokines and Th1, Th2, Th17, and Treg-associated genes; several within-group changes were observed, with limited between-group effects.
Focused review summarizes immune-system regulation by vitamin D, VDR evidence, deficiency studies, and supplementation trials in Hashimoto's and Graves' disease.
Cross-sectional study associates the VDR FokI genotype with Hashimoto's and suggests possible receptor dysfunction, but does not directly evaluate immune-cell regulation or inflammatory mediators.
